source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Mosaic virus disease transmitted by planthopper (ជម្ងឺគៀលឡើង, Mosaic Virus): this disease is transmitted by an insect vector named Peregrinus maidis, a type of planthopper/leafhopper (Leaf hopper). Damage tends to appear at the early growth stage of the corn plant, particularly when the crop is young, causing the plant's overall health and leaves to decline in vigor. At that stage the corn plant may also be attacked by other insects, but this virus itself cannot be treated once infection occurs.

This disease has no specific chemical cure; the following practices are recommended:
- Select and plant clean seed with no history of the disease.
- Use resistant/tolerant varieties.
- Sanitize field tools appropriately.
- Plant at an appropriate time that avoids periods of high risk associated with vector insect population buildup.
- Uproot infected plants showing clear virus symptoms and dispose of them away from the field.
